title: n view of the possibility of unrest during the students’ proposed march to the state assembly, the police administration has been put on alert, ADG (Headquarters) Manoj Kaushik said
author: PTI
content_html:
The Jharkhand Police has imposed prohibitory orders around the assembly premises and made elaborate security arrangements across the city in view of Monday's (August 10, 2026) 'Vidhan Sabha March' called by students who have been protesting for more than two weeks against alleged irregularities in recruitment exams in the state.

BJP leader Amar Bauri alleged on Sunday (August 9) that the party's State unit president Aditya Sahu has been "put under house arrest".

Mr. Bauri, also the party's state general secretary, said the government will "not be able to achieve success by deploying security personnel outside Mr. Sahu’s residence".

All necessary security arrangements are being made in view of the proposed picketing at the state assembly, the officer said.

“In view of the possibility of unrest during the students’ proposed march to the state assembly, the police administration has been put on alert,” ADG (Headquarters) Manoj Kaushik said.

He urged the students, who will participate in the march to protest in a "peaceful and disciplined" manner as they have shown their discipline in the ongoing protest here for over two weeks, he said.

"It is their responsibility to ensure that anti-social elements and troublemakers are prevented from joining the march," the ADG said.

Ranchi SSP Rakesh Ranjan said that maintaining law and order during the march is everyone’s responsibility.

"We do not want a blot on the career of any student due to disruption of law and order. Barricades have been put in place at major points with the deployment of adequate police force across the city," the SSP said.

A prohibitory order has already been promulgated within a 750-metre radius of the Vidhan Sabha building from August 6 to 12. The order will be in place between 6 a.m. and 10 p.m. on these days, he said.

Such an order was also imposed from Sunday (August 9) midnight in Jamshedpur in view of the protest march in Ranchi, an official statement said.

The Ranchi district administration has made an appeal to agitating students to refrain from participating in any kind of aggressive demonstrations.

It also cautioned against violence and illegal activities during the protest march to the assembly.

Protesters alleged that hundreds of students coming to the state capital from different parts of Jharkhand were being stopped by the police forcefully.

The students' protest entered its 16th day on Sunday (August 9), while six of them are on hunger strike protesting against alleged irregularities in recruitment exams.

Published - August 10, 2026 09:09 am IST

    Thousands of student protestors participate in 'Vidhan Sabha Gherao' march

  • August 10, 2026 11:31
    Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader Devendra Nath Mahto joins march

    Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who has been on a hunger strike for nine days in protest against exam irregularities, joined the march in an ambulance, despite losing 10.5 kg. He was seen carrying a portrait of former Chief Minister Shibu Soren.- PTI

    'Until our demands are met, we will not stop', says protestor

    A student participating in Vidhan Sabha gherao march, said, “We have been stopped here but we will head towards the Vidhan Sabha peacefully. Until our demands are met, we will not stop. We demand CBI investigation...”- ANI

  • August 10, 2026 11:20
    ED initiates probe into Jharkhand PSC exams irregularities case

    The Enforcement Directorate has launched an investigation into alleged irregularities in the conduct of multiple recruitment examinations in Jharkhand particularly the JSSC-CGL examination, officials said on Monday (August 10, 2026).

    They said the central agency has taken cognisance of a state police CID FIR and some other complaints to initiate a probe under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).

    Students have been agitating in the State for 16 days demanding a CBI probe into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations, particularly the JSSC-CGL (Jharkhand General Graduate Level Combined Competitive Examination).- PTI

  • August 10, 2026 11:18
    Protestors peacefully marching towards assembly with volunteers forming human chain ahead of them

    Protestors are peacefully marching towards the State assembly with volunteers forming human chain ahead of them. Jharkhand Police’s water canon vehicle and riot control vehicle are present at the site.- Aniket Singh Chauhan, Suruchi Kumari

    WhatsApp Image 2026-08-10 at 11.14.20 AM.jpeg

    Photo credit: Suruchi Kumari

    Police detain BJP leaders, including Aditya Sahu and Babulal Marandi

    Police detain BJP leaders, including Aditya Sahu and Babulal Marandi, protesting outside CM Hemant Soren’s residence over exam irregularities.

    BJP’s Jharkhand unit spokesperson Pratul Shahdeo said he, several other leaders are under house arrest since 7 a.m.- PTI

  • August 10, 2026 10:31
    Student appeals to the people of Jharkhand to extend their moral support

    Student leader Ravindra Paswan said ahead of the march to assembly on Monday (August 10), “All of us are gathering at the Old Vidhan Sabha. We will begin our march from there in a very peaceful and constitutional manner. I would like to appeal to all the students to do this in a very peaceful and constitutional manner. I also appeal to the common public of Jharkhand to extend us their moral support. I also appeal to the CM to meet our demands, all our demands are genuine.”- ANI

  • August 10, 2026 10:27
    Protestors start gathering for march to State Assembly

    The march to the State Assembly is yet to begin but people have started to gather outside the main gate of Old Vidhan Sabha.

    Jharkhand police personnel are deployed along the Dhurva road leading to the old Vidhan Sabha from where the ‘Vidhan Sabha Gherao’ march is set to begin towards the the new Vidhan Sabha. 

    Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is in effect within a 750-metre radius of the State Assembly as per the Monsoon Session schedule from August 6 to August 12. It bars the assembly of five or more persons, processions, rallies, demonstrations and public meetings in the notified area.- Aniket Singh Chauhan, Suruchi Kumari

  • August 10, 2026 10:14
    For Jharkhand’s Adivasi youth, competitive exams are about finding a voice in the system that governs them

    For many, JPSC and JSSC represent perhaps the clearest route to secure employment in a State where the private sector offers limited opportunities, particularly for young people from rural and Adivasi communities.

    The choice, as several aspirants describe it, is stark: continue tilling the land that often provides enough to sustain a family but little surplus or spend years studying for a competitive examination that can potentially change the family’s economic circumstances.

  • August 10, 2026 09:51
    'Government has not fulfilled even five per cent of our demands', says student on hunger strike

    Student protestor Savita Kumari said, “We had planned not to march towards the Assembly if the government fulfills our demands. But the government has not fulfilled even five per cent of our demands. So, all our brothers and sisters are marching towards the Assembly today to gherao it... We are protesting here and are on hunger strike.”- PTI

    Students remain firm on their demand for a CBI probe into the irregularities in JSSC-CGL examination

    The Jharkhand government on Sunday (August 9, 2026) agreed to cancel the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) preliminary examination and the JPSC backlog examinations held in 2023 and 2025 following six hours of discussions with protesting student groups.

    However, the students remained firm on their demand for a CBI probe into the irregularities in the JSSC-CGL examination and said the agitation would continue. The announcement came even as all three JPSC members resigned and Chief Minister Hemant Soren assured protestors that “justice will be delivered with full transparency”.

    Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha (JLKM) and JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, said they want cancellation of JSSC-CGL and all exams connected to the TSR Data Processing Private Limited Agency, a blacklisted entity.

    “In view of the possibility of unrest during the students’ proposed march to the State assembly, the police administration has been put on alert,” ADG (Headquarters) Manoj Kaushik said.

    He urged the students, who will participate in the march to protest in a “peaceful and disciplined” manner as they have shown their discipline in the ongoing protest here for over two weeks, he said.

    Students from every district of Jharkhand are arriving for today's protest: Student leader Ravindra Paswan

    Student leader Ravindra Paswan said ahead of the march to Assembly, “A march to the Vidhan Sabha and a gherao will be conducted in a peaceful and constitutional manner. Students will start gathering there at 9:00 a.m.. The march will commence between 10:30 and 11:00 a.m., entirely peacefully and constitutionally. I urge all students and the general public to maintain peace and adhere to constitutional norms. Since we students are leading this movement, we must demonstrate that we are disciplined and educated. Students from every district of Jharkhand are arriving for today’s protest; there will be a massive turnout.”- ANI

    Students leave for the old Jharkhand Legislative Assembly building

    Protesting students leave from Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium for the old Jharkhand Legislative Assembly building, ahead of their call for Vidhan Sabha march to the new Assembly on Monday (August 10, 2026).- ANI

  • August 10, 2026 09:30
    Ranchi prepares for march to state Assembly today

    Student protesters are set to hold a ‘Vidhan Sabha Gherao’ march in Ranchi today (Monday) over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) and Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) examinations, with security arrangements tightened across the city.

    The Jharkhand Police and administration have made elaborate security arrangements ahead of the march, with razor fencing installed along the route near Jagannath Temple. Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) has also been imposed within a 750-metre radius of the state Assembly.- ANI

title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 16 LIVE: Lok Sabha to take up introduction of four key bills, including Tribunals Reforms Bill today
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
• outside parliament
    August 10, 2026 12:21
    Deadlock in Parliament will continue till HM Shah gives statement: Priyanka Gandhi

    Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Monday asserted that the deadlock between the opposition and the government in Parliament will continue till Union Home Minister Amit Shah makes a statement over alleged police excesses on students.

    With only four days of the Monsoon session remaining, the fate of major bills on women’s reservation, delimitation and the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act (FCRA) remains uncertain amid the ongoing logjam in Parliament.

    None of these Bills figured in the list of business for the Lok Sabha for Monday.

    “I think the deadlock in Parliament will continue till the Union Home Minister gives a statement,” Ms. Priyanka Gandhi told reporters in the Parliament House complex.

    -PTI

  • rajya sabha
    August 10, 2026 12:20

    With protests from the Opposition, the Rajya Sabha was adjourned till 2 p.m.

    Lok Sabha proceedings were adjourned till 2 p.m. on Monday amid noisy protest by the Opposition, which is seeking a response from the government on police action on protesting students and alleged theft of Ram temple donations. 

    Lok Sabha proceedings have witnessed repeated disruptions all throughout the Monsoon Session with six out of eight bills being passed by the House without a debate. Monday was the 16th day when the House could not complete the Question Hour, which is held between 11 am and 12 noon. 

    Four Bills were introduced -- The Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026, the Minerals and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 and The National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026.

    Opposition MPs, including Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, protested in Parliament House complex on Monday over the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya and the “police excesses” against student protesters.

    They demanded that Home Minister Amit Shah must come to Parliament and make a statement on the alleged police excesses during the July 20 student protest over the paper leak issue.

    Carrying placards against the government, the MPs protested in front of the Makar Dwar of Parliament with slogans such as ‘chhanda chor, gaddi chor’, ‘Amit Shah jawaab do’ and ‘chanda chor kahan milenge, BJP ke daftar mein’.

    The MPs also kept a donation box at the spot to symbolise the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple and lined up around them to raise slogans against the government.

    As per the list of business, the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, will be introduced by Union Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal. The Bill seeks to improve the functioning of tribunals and ensure transparency and uniformity in the appointment and service conditions of tribunal members. It also proposes setting up a National Tribunals Commission. 

    The House will also take up the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. Union Minister G Kishan Reddy will move for leave to introduce the Bill, which seeks to further amend the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act, 1957.

    Floor leaders of the Opposition parties will hold a meeting in the chamber of the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha, Mallikarjun Kharge, to chalk out the strategy for the Floor of the House on Monday.

    The INDIA bloc MPs are likely to continue their protest against the alleged Ram Mandir donation embezzlement and demand Union Home Minister Amit Shah’s statement on the police action against protesters in Delhi on July 20.

    While Congress MP Manickam Tagore has moved an adjournment motion in the Lok Sabha, seeking Amit Shah’s statement, KC Venugopal has sought a discussion on the Ram Mandir donation row.

    The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026 is also expected to be taken up in the discussion of the Opposition leaders.

title: Kanwar Yatra 2026: Traffic restrictions in Delhi, U.P., and Haryana
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
Kanwar Yatra, or the annual pilgrimage of people from the Ganges River to their local temples, is underway and will conclude on Tuesday (August 11, 2026).

The festive pilgrimage began on July 30 and will conclude on August 11, 2026 on the day of Shivratri.

U.P. CM Yogi showers flowers on Kanwariyas, describes Kanwar Yatra as unparalleled example of devotion, unity 

Owing to the heavy pedestrian and pilgrimage traffic, specific advisories have been issued by authorities to ease commute of citizens, especially in Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, and Haryana.

Here’s your guide to what’s open and what’s closed.

Region/StateAffected areas and restrictionsDuration of restrictionsRecommended Alternate Routes
Delhi• Kalindi Kunj junction, Okhla Barrage road, Noida–Kalindi Kunj road, and Okhla Bird Sanctuary • GT Road (Apsara Border to Yamuna Bridge) closed for general trafficAugust 11–12, 2026• Avoid Kalindi Kunj, GT Road, and Wazirabad Road. • Use designated alternate corridors like NH-9 and NH-44.
Gurugram (Haryana)• Heavy vehicle movement entering Delhi via Haridwar return paths • Travel corridors toward Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, and FaridabadAugust 9 – 11, 2026• Use Dwarka Expressway. • Use KMP Expressway via Panchgaon Chowk.
Ghaziabad (Uttar Pradesh)• Delhi-Meerut Expressway (DME) • Heavy pilgrim traffic on NH-58 / Delhi-Meerut routeAugust 9 – 12, 2026•Use NH-09 as primary alternative route • Siddharth Vihar to Meerut Tiraha: Take NH-09, Vijayanagar Cut, Overbridge, and Chaudhary Mod.

Delhi 

The Delhi Traffic Police, in a post on X on August 10, 2026, said that “traffic congestion is likely on Kalindi Kunj junction, Okhla Barrage road, Noida, Kalindi Kunj-Noida road and the connecting roads towards Okhla Bird Sanctuary.” It especially warned commuters not to use the routes leading through Kalindi Kunj junction, to plan commutes in advance and to allow sufficient additional travel time.

Delhi CM assures kanwariyas will not face any difficulties

TRAFFIC ADVISORY

Traffic movement in and around Kalindi Kunj Junction is likely to remain slow and congested till 12.08.2026 due to heavy movement of Kanwariyas during the ongoing Kanwar Yatra and ongoing road repair work on the Okhla Barrage–Kalindi Kunj stretch.

📍ADVISORY… pic.twitter.com/dzqYI092mO

— Delhi Traffic Police (@dtptraffic) August 9, 2026

Gurugram, Haryana

Gurugram traffic police, on August 8, detailed alternate routes for heavy vehicles to take to enter the national capital of Delhi owing to the ‘Kanwar Yatra’ pilgrimage and the return of the ‘kanwariyas’ from Haridwar.

School van vandalised in Lucknow allegedly by Kanwariyas 

 It asked commuters to “use Dwarka and KMP expressway via Panchgaon Chowk” as travel corridors to Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, and Faridabad may also be affected.

This advisory is in effect till August 11, 2026 and the traffic police also attached maps for easy referencing for citizens.

Heavy Vehicle Advisory (9–11 Aug)
Kanwariyas return from Haridwar for jalabhishek on Mahashivratri, 11 Aug.
· Use Dwarka & KMP Expressway via Panchgaon Chowk
· For Rajasthan, Jhajjar, Rewari, Pataudi, Nuh, Faridabad
📞 112 | 1095#TrafficAdvisory#KMPExpressway#RoadSafetypic.twitter.com/QNABiSDIuF

— Gurugram Traffic Police (@TrafficGGM) August 8, 2026

Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh

Ghaziabad in Uttar Pradesh is also under a traffic advisory by the traffic police. An X post, with a video by Varun Kumar Singh, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic), said that “For the safe movement of Kanwar devotees, the Delhi-Meerut Expressway (DME) will be restricted for general traffic on August 10 and 11, 2026.” It added that: In view of the large number of Kanwar pilgrims on NH-58/Delhi-Meerut route, use Rapid Metro (RRTS) and public transport instead of private vehicles, and use NH-09 as much as possible.

Traffic curbs for Kanwar Yatra in U.P.’s Muzaffarnagar till August 12

Vehicles coming from Siddharth Vihar to Meerut Tiraha should use NH-09, Vijayanagar Cut, Overbridge, and Chaudhary Mod.” 

It advised locals to use NH-09 instead for commuting. 

#GhaziabadTrafficPolice#KanwarYatra2026

🚦कांवड़ यात्रा-2026 के दृष्टिगत कांवड़ यात्रियों की भारी संख्या को देखते हुए दिनांक 10.08.2026 एवं 11.08.2026 को यातायात एडवाइजरी व रूट डायवर्जन सूचना संबंधी वीडियो बाइट🚦

👉 कांवड़ श्रद्धालुओं के सुरक्षित आवागमन हेतु 10 व 11 अगस्त… pic.twitter.com/gjKWuGeiG4

— Ghaziabad Traffic Police (@Gzbtrafficpol) August 9, 2026

What is Kanwar Yatra?

Kanwar Yatra is an annual pilgrimage where devotees of Lord Shiva collect holy water from the Ganges River from places like Haridawar, Gangotri, Gaumukh, or Sultanganj and take it to their local temples, often walking barefoot for long distances.

It occurs during July-August, depending on the Hindu calendar month of ‘Shravan.’
